Expectation1: Secure packages and confirm successful delivery
Situation1: Leaving a package safely at the doorstep when no one is home
Expectation2: Raise public awareness about social inequities and marginalized groups
Situation2: They respond to an urgent incident of discrimination that requires immediate public attention and awareness.
Story: I balanced the heavy box in my arms, scanning the quiet street for any sign of the recipient. As a delivery person, my job was clear: make sure the package reached the right doorstep, safe and sound, even if no one was home. I snapped a photo for proof, but as I was about to leave, my phone buzzed with an urgent message. A friend from the advocacy group sent a video—someone in our community was being harassed, right now, just a few blocks away. My heart pounded. I was supposed to be there, raising my voice, documenting, making sure the world saw what was happening. But I still had three more deliveries, and this package couldn’t be left unattended for long. I felt the weight of both roles pressing down on me: the expectation to protect someone’s belongings, and the responsibility to stand up for someone’s dignity. I stood on the porch, torn, the package in my hands and the call for justice ringing in my ears, unsure which duty I could afford to let down.
